title: Still, God may have added supernatural gifts; Scripture is clear only that he revealed himself to Adam
source_text: LVII. Verum inde non sequitur falsum esse quod diserte docent Reformati complures, nimirum in primo homine fuisse dona quaedam supernaturalia. Nam potuit Deus ad naturae primigeniae dotes, & auxilia ei necessaria, supra naturam quod libuit addere; sed quid illud & quantum fuerit, non audemus, scriptura tacente, definire. Illud tamen ex scriptura certum, in primo homine fuisse notitiam quandam supernaturalem: quandoquidem Deus illi supra naturam sese revelavit, & de voluntate sua expresso verbo illum edocuit.
pass_a_gloss: But it does not follow thence that what many Reformed expressly teach is false, namely that there were in the first man certain supernatural gifts. For God could add to the endowments of primeval nature, and the aids necessary to it, what he pleased above nature; but what that was and how much, we do not dare, scripture being silent, to define. This however is certain from scripture, that there was in the first man a certain supernatural knowledge: since God revealed himself to him above nature, and taught him about his will by express word.
pass_b_english: It does not follow, however, that what many of the Reformed explicitly teach is false, namely that the first man had some supernatural gifts. God could have added to the endowments of man's first nature, and to the help it needed, whatever he pleased above nature. But what that was and how much, we do not venture to define, since Scripture is silent.
One thing Scripture does make certain: the first man had a certain supernatural knowledge, since God revealed himself to him beyond nature and taught him his will in express words.

choices.why: Le Blanc means spoken command, as in Genesis 2:16-17.
